Source size: as first produced, the workspace was about 470 MB as a gzipped tar, mostly kernel-checked certificate data. For this submission the files outside the import closure were dropped, and the 2612 certificate bodies in the GlobalRepellingData*.lean files are written as `fast_case% "..."`, a compact decimal form that a syntax macro (Submission/Codec/FastCase.lean) expands back to exactly the same terms. The compact form stores each disk centre as a branch choice (0 or 1) plus a small correction to the exact preimage of the matching disk of the previous step, and leaves out the five check bounds of each cell, which the macro recomputes as the tightest values the checker accepts (the values every certificate already stored). Every certificate is still checked by `decide +kernel`, and no axioms are added. The submitted tree is 26.8 MB as a gzipped tar; the commit message lists the changes.

Produced by Humanfia's LOT (Lean Option Tree) orchestrator: agent sessions recursively split the statement into frozen sub-obligations, prove them in parallel, and every step is checked with the official lean-eval checker (comparator, nanoda and Lean kernel replay). The proof is fully machine-written; humans built the orchestrator and the seed package, chose the external code the run could use, and operated the infrastructure. It follows the route of Pardon's proof (J. Amer. Math. Soc. 26 (2013)).

Builds on Mathlib and lean-pool, which is imported as a dependency (projects imported: Brouwer, ClassificationOfSurfaces, FiniteGraphFundamentalGroup, HopfProblem, JacobianDiffgeo, PLAcceleratedNesterovLean, Polytopes, RiemannMappingTheorem, SardMoreira, Schoenflies). Some files of the proof contain code copied or adapted from lean-pool projects (Brouwer, ClassificationOfSurfaces, EhrhartVolumeInequality, FiniteGraphFundamentalGroup, HopfProblem, JacobianDiffgeo, SardMoreira, Schoenflies), and four files are modified copies of, or new code around, three files on cell triangulations from OpenAI's `openai/math` repository (Apache-2.0). Each such file keeps its copyright and attribution header. `NOTICE` at the tree's root lists the imported libraries, every piece of copied or adapted code with its licence, and where each of those files now is; the licence texts are in `LICENSES/` (lean-pool's LICENSE, Brouwer's MIT licence, and the NOTICE and LICENSE that come with the cell-triangulation code).

The submitted tree holds only the import closure of the theorem's module: 5271 Lean files under `Submission/`. To fit the evaluation's 4-core time limit, they are joined into 1083 modules: 4672 files form 484 merged modules, and 599 files are kept as they are. Files are joined only along their imports, and only when every file that imports one of them already imports all of them, so no module sees more names than before. Each joined file's text appears unchanged between the lines `-- ====== begin <original path> ======` and `-- ====== end <original path> ======`: first its header comments, then its text after the imports, inside its own `section ... end` (with an `end` added for each section or namespace the file leaves open). The statement and every proof are unchanged. Size: 1099 files, 9.67 MB as a gzipped tar.

Checked before submission with the official comparator setup (comparator d03acab, lean4export 076e8e5, nanoda 68d5ca9, Lean kernel replay; permitted axioms propext, Quot.sound, Classical.choice) in an isolated container: "Your solution is okay!" for this tree (with the problem's `PROBLEM.md`, which the checker expects; the submitted tree leaves it out as in our other submissions). This check took 43 min at 16 CPUs (container memory peak 21.3 GiB). Measured on a runner-sized container (4 CPUs, 15 GB memory, Lean-Eval's layout with lean-pool built from source), the whole check took 2 h 47 min (2 h 25 min of it compiling), with a comparator peak of 8.0 GiB and at most 3.5 GiB for any single Lean process.
